thread.title: Nasdaq Today Leads Bounce As Holiday Shopping Leaps | Investor's Business Daily

author: JUAN CARLOS ARANCIBIA
title: Nasdaq Today Leads Bounce As Holiday Shopping Leaps | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The Nasdaq today jumped sharply and held near session highs in midafternoon trade, spearheading a rebound in the stock market that saw consumer and retail sectors bask in the glow of a strong holiday shopping season.
X In late afternoon trading, the Nasdaq composite surged 5%, while the S&P 500 rose 4.2% and the Dow Jones industrial average climbed 4.3%. All three are on pace to snap a damaging four-day losing streak that left the Nasdaq and S&P 500 low enough to be considered in a bear market.
Volume at 1 p.m. ET was lower compared with the same time Monday. The market closed early at that hour Monday, which means today's trading is lagging even after discounting the shortened Monday session.
Indexes extended gains in afternoon trading.
Microsoft ( MSFT ) rose 5.4% and was a big reason the Nasdaq composite outperformed. Microsoft is now the stock with highest market capitalization after former No. 1 Apple ( AAPL ) took a thrashing. But like so many tech stocks, Microsoft is trading below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, searching for a bottom.
The Nasdaq led major indexes even though only 21% of the composite is made up of consumer stocks , which were the top sectors Wednesday. Strength in technology (45% of the Nasdaq) and health care (11%) helped the Nasdaq lead.
On the Dow Jones industrial average, Home Depot ( HD ), Nike ( NKE ), Visa ( V ) and Walmart ( WMT ) were Dow components up more than 4.5% as consumer stocks outperformed in the waning days of the holiday shopping season.
Retail, Consumer Sectors Lead Retail and consumer discretionary were Wednesday's best sectors. The SPDR S&P Retail ETF ( XRT ) and Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR Fund ( XLY ) each climbed about 4.5%.
Holiday retail sales grew at the fastest pace in six years , according to Mastercard SpendingPulse.
Amazon.com ( AMZN ), the largest online retailer and former longtime member of IBD Leaderboard , gushed about record holiday sales. Amazon shares bounced nearly 6% but remain 30% below their prior high. Amazon's rally was the main reason IBD's internet retail industry group climbed more than 7% to top the industry table.
Energy stocks also were leading, with exploration & production, refinery and drilling among the top 30 of 197 industry groups. The crude oil price leapt more than 7% to $45.63 a barrel.
The battered small caps also rallied, with the Russell 2000 up 4.1%.
There was some relief on Wall Street after the White House eased worries that President Trump was anxious to fire Fed Chairman Jerome Powell. Kevin Hassett, chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers, told the Wall Street Journal that Powell's job is "100% safe."
